Subject: Urgent: offline delta push (v2.1) — need signing + operator instructions

Jasmine —

We have a high-severity fix that needs to be pushed to 28 on-prem units that are air-gapped. Because these devices cannot reach the internet, our field techs will apply a signed delta bundle delivered on USB. We need: 1) a validated signing procedure and artifacts we can verify offline, 2) a short step-by-step operator checklist for acceptance testing, and 3) evidence artifacts (signed manifest) for our compliance team.

Attached: acme_patch_v2.1.tar.gz and the raw patch produced by our SRE. We can coordinate secure courier for hardware where necessary. Please advise on the recommended HSM-backed signing flow and any minimum verification commands the operator should run before activation.

Time is sensitive — we are targeting 2026-01-21 as the earliest field window.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Ops Manager, Acme Medical Systems
ops@acmemedica.com

Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: offline delta push (v2.1) — need signing + operator instructions

Thanks Daniel — copying the on-call team. High level answers up front: we can produce an HSM-attested signature for the delta, publish a signed manifest, and provide a concise operator checklist for offline verification. Below is a proposed minimal plan so we can align quickly.

Plan (short):
- Security will sign the artifact with our HSM key and produce two artifacts: (1) artifact.tar.gz.sig and (2) signed_manifest-<date>.json.sig that includes SHA256 checksums and approved rollout window.
- Field operators receive: artifact.tar.gz, artifact.tar.gz.sig, signed_manifest.json.sig, and operator_checklist.pdf.
- Operator checklist includes pre-check hashes, a signed-manifest verification step, and rollback instruction.
- For compliance we'll export a signed attestation bundle (timestamped) and share to audits@datatrust.io.

Open questions:
1) Does Acme require double-signing (customer-side signing) or is Redwood single HSM signature sufficient?
2) Will operators have an SSH-enabled jump host on-site to run verification commands, or must everything be purely offline (no network)?

Action items: priyom to produce the HSM workflow and manifest template; ben to draft the operator checklist and quick acceptance tests; marissa to own packaging and courier labeling.

If this plan looks OK we'll fast-track.

—
Jasmine Liu
Partner Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, ops@acmemedica.com
Cc: audits@datatrust.io
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 08:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: offline delta push (v2.1) — need signing + operator instructions

Jasmine / Daniel —

Below is the HSM-backed signing and verification flow I recommend for a purely offline acceptance path. I've included the exact CLI checks to put in the operator checklist.

HSM signing flow (Redwood):
1) SRE uploads the canonical delta artifact to our secure build queue (internal only).
2) We produce canonical SHA256 checksum and confirm size/manifest.
3) The artifact is loaded into the signing enclave (HSM) and signed with the "redwood-release" key. The HSM produces: artifact.tar.gz.sig and manifest.json.sig containing: version, artifact_sha256, truncated HSM cert serial, timestamp, and approved roll window.
4) We then produce an attestation bundle (attestation.zip) that includes the HSM certificate chain and signature timestamp for compliance export.

Operator offline verification commands (to be run locally on the appliance or jump host):
- sha256sum acme_patch_v2.1.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}'  # verify checksum equals <artifact_sha256>
- openssl dgst -sha256 -verify redwood_pubkey.pem -signature acme_patch_v2.1.tar.gz.sig acme_patch_v2.1.tar.gz
- openssl dgst -sha256 -verify redwood_pubkey.pem -signature signed_manifest-20260118.json.sig signed_manifest-20260118.json

If devices have no ability to import redwood_pubkey.pem, operators should verify against the signed_manifest which itself contains the expected artifact_sha256 and is signed by us. The CLI above uses the published public key file that we will include on the courier in PEM format.

Rollback / safety notes:
- If any checksum or signature verification fails, operators must quarantine the media and call the Redwood on-call number.
- Do not execute the installer binary if the signed_manifest indicates a different version or an out-of-window timestamp.

I will attach: signed_manifest template (signed_manifest-20260118.json.sig), and a sample attestation bundle for audits.

—
Priyom Das
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
[Attachment: signed_manifest-20260118.json.sig]

- Acceptance tests (to include in checklist): 1) SHA256 check; 2) signature verification of artifact and manifest; 3) boot smoke test (service starts and healthcheck returns 200); 4) sample inference sanity test using the local test vector (we'll include a small test payload).
- Courier: patchsupplies@securecourier.com can ship sealed USB kits. We need recipient POC for each site and a signed handoff form.

Windows:

-Ben
